33.43000,35.13000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
33.43000,35.13000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-95.51230,29.78360.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Sonja B. Kristiansen, MD. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. -59.67738,-33.67630.name: Centro MÃ©dico FERTILAB
-59.67738,-33.67630.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.fertilab.com.ar. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

126.65600,45.62800.name: Chinese National High Containment Facilities for Animal Diseases Control and Prevention, Harbin Veterinary Research Institute
126.65600,45.62800.state: No.678 Heping Road, Xiangfang District, Harbin 150069, P.R.China, China
126.65600,45.62800.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Operational or announced: 2018. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-74.45900,40.45200.name: Genomic Prediction / LifeView
-74.45900,40.45200.desc: Sells polygenic risk scoring of IVF embryos, including for traits with no single genetic cause. Professional genetics bodies have said the science does not support clinical use. It is sold regardless, because embryo selection requires none of the approval a drug or device would need — the distance between what the evidence supports and what may lawfully be sold is the entire market.

28.22930,-25.74790.name: Executive Council for GMOs — Department of Agriculture
28.22930,-25.74790.desc: South Africa’s GMO decision body, in the country that grows more engineered maize than anywhere else in Africa and where white maize — the staple people eat directly, not livestock feed — is largely engineered. Most engineered maize worldwide goes to animals. Here it is dinner, which makes South Africa the place where the food-safety argument is least abstract.

28.22930,-25.74790.name: Executive Council: GMO Act (South Africa)
28.22930,-25.74790.desc: The body that authorises releases in the biggest engineered-crop producer in Africa, sitting under the agriculture department with a separate appeal board above it. It approved open field trials of drought-tolerant maize in 2007, extended them in 2010 and granted commercial release in 2015 — and in 2024 the Supreme Court of Appeal set that chain of decisions aside. Read it alongside the Brazilian council and the Indian committee already on this map: three countries, three different structures for who signs off a release, and in each the interesting question is not the science but who checks the body that checked the applicant.

9.94300,52.13700.name: KWS SAAT
9.94300,52.13700.desc: A German seed company, family-controlled, with a dominant position in sugar beet and a large one in maize. European breeders of this size operate under rules that make engineered crops commercially impossible to sell domestically, so their engineered work happens abroad or not at all.

-93.43800,44.90600.name: Cargill
-93.43800,44.90600.desc: The largest privately held company in the United States, trading and processing a very large share of the world's grain, oilseed and animal feed. Being private means it discloses almost nothing: no quarterly filings, no shareholder meeting, no obligation to explain a sourcing decision. Almost every engineered commodity crop grown anywhere passes through a trader of this kind, and traders are regulated as merchants rather than as participants in biotechnology.
